numeric_changes.source_excerpt: 23.6%与23.9%相差0.3个百分点，不能据此宣布AI和真人“统计等效”。愿意进入AI应用的人，可能本来就更接受这种表现方式；两款应用也可能有不同的免费入口、付费墙、流量定向和内容类型。2737名某应用用户不能代表全体美国观众，更不能拿这份问卷样本量，替代两款应用转化率各自的样本量。这里最稳妥的结论是：运营商观察到了某些AI内容用户的实际付费行为；“观众不会为AI剧付钱”已经不是一个可以不加检验地采用的前提。
numeric_changes.english_excerpt: The 0.3-percentage-point difference between 23.6% and 23.9% does not establish “statistical equivalence” between AI and live action. People willing to enter an AI app may already be more receptive to its presentation; the two apps may also differ in free entry points, paywalls, traffic targeting, and content types. A sample of 2737 users of one app cannot represent the entire US audience, and that survey sample cannot substitute for the respective sample sizes behind the two apps' conversion rates. The most defensible conclusion is that the operator observed actual payments by some AI-content users. “Audiences will not pay for AI dramas” can no longer be adopted as an untested premise.

numeric_changes.source_excerpt: 截至本轮，最值得重视的是入门入口收窄，而非已经证明程序员整体大规模消失。Stanford的2026年8月12日修订研究使用截至6月的ADP行政工资数据，覆盖数百万美国工作者；22—25岁高AI暴露职业的就业，相对若跟随低暴露同龄人轨迹的路径落后19%，经验较多者没有同样缺口。作者将主要分化归于招聘减少，未发现全经济普遍替代。年龄不等于资历，高暴露职业不只包括程序员；19%是相对路径差，不是“初级程序员被裁19%”。控制后仍存在的分化值得重视，但教育、招聘周期、样本与预趋势使它不能被当作已识别的AI净因果比例。[Stanford原论文，2026年8月版](https://digitaleconomy.stanford.edu/app/uploads/2026/08/Canaries_August2026.pdf)
numeric_changes.english_excerpt: The most important evidence at this review date concerns narrowing entry-level hiring, rather than proof of broad large-scale disappearance of programmers. Stanford's revised study of 12 August 2026 uses ADP administrative payroll data through June covering millions of US workers. Employment of 22–25-year-olds in highly AI-exposed occupations lagged by 19% relative to the path it would have followed alongside less-exposed peers of the same age; more-experienced workers had no comparable gap. The authors attribute the main divergence to reduced hiring and do not find general economy-wide replacement. Age is not experience, and highly exposed occupations include more than programmers. The 19% is a relative-path gap, not “19% of junior programmers laid off.” Divergence remaining after controls deserves attention, but education, hiring cycles, the sample, and pretrends prevent it from being treated as an identified net causal AI percentage. [Stanford original paper, August 2026 version](https://digitaleconomy.stanford.edu/app/uploads/2026/08/Canaries_August2026.pdf)

numeric_changes.source_excerpt: 另一项美国数据提供方向上的补强。Fed研究者Crane与Soto在3月20日工作论文中，以O*NET定义编程密集职业并联结CPS，控制行业层面冲击后，ChatGPT出现后的程序员就业年增长趋势比此前低约3个百分点；总人数仍增长。它比单看科技公司裁员更接近职业需求，也没有把所有减速都归给行业衰退；但以2022年末作为事件断点、无法完整排除同期职业冲击，仍不足以把差额全部归因AI。研究者观点也不等于美联储官方预测。[Fed原始论文](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/feds/files/2026018pap.pdf)
numeric_changes.english_excerpt: Another US dataset provides directional corroboration. In a 20 March working paper, Federal Reserve researchers Crane and Soto define programming-intensive occupations using O*NET and link them to CPS. After controlling for industry-level shocks, programmers' annual employment-growth trend after ChatGPT's arrival was approximately 3 percentage points below its previous trend; total employment still grew. This is closer to occupational demand than simply tracking technology-company layoffs and does not attribute all slowing to an industry downturn. But using late 2022 as the event breakpoint cannot fully exclude contemporaneous occupational shocks and remains insufficient to attribute the entire difference to AI. Researchers' views are also not an official Federal Reserve forecast. [Original Federal Reserve paper](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/feds/files/2026018pap.pdf)

numeric_changes.english_excerpt: Epoch/Ipsos adds a direct survey signal of task transfers. A probability-sample survey conducted on 10–19 July 2026 included 1106 employed US adults, with 1103 retained after quality control. Approximately 20% said at least one task previously assigned to a colleague or contractor was now assigned to AI. This is not “20% of jobs replaced,” nor a coding-specific sample, and the answers do not establish whether the former colleague became unemployed. It nevertheless shows that work-allocation boundaries are changing. Such task transfers may first reduce outsourced orders and new hiring, then gradually affect the stock of jobs. [Epoch original results](https://epoch.ai/publications/one-in-five-workers-delegate-work-to-ai), [Ipsos sample description](https://www.ipsos.com/en-us/epoch-ai-ipsos-august-2026-poll)
